Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 1:

(p-484) Surah "The Hypocrites" (al-Munafiqun)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."﴾ They intended a testimony in which their hearts did not agree with their tongues.

﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger.﴾ That is: Allah knows that the matter is as their words indicate: ﴿that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah.﴾ ﴿And Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars﴾ in their claim of agreement between heart and tongue. Or, they are liars in it, because if it is devoid of agreement of heart, it is not a testimony in reality, so they are liars in calling it a testimony. Or: they are liars in their own estimation, because they believed that their saying "You are indeed the Messenger of Allah" was a lie, and it was a report contrary to the actual state of the one it reports about.

Tafsir al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 63, verse 2:

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, a protection from being taken captive and from being killed. In this is evidence that "I bear witness" (ashhadu) is an oath (yamin),

﴿and so they have barred﴾, [they have barred] the people,

﴿from the way of Allah﴾, from Islam, by causing aversion and by casting doubts,

﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾, [namely] their hypocrisy and their barring of people from the way of Allah. And in "evil" (saa'a) there is the meaning of wonder (ta'ajjub), which is the magnification of their affair in the minds of the listeners.

ذَلِكَ (That) refers to His saying: "Evil is what they have been doing" (ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ), meaning: that statement bearing witness against them that they are the worst of people in their deeds.

بِأنَّهُمْ (because they),
i.e., because of the fact that

آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا (they believed and then disbelieved). Or it refers to what He described of their state in hypocrisy, lying, and concealing themselves behind oaths (p-485). That is: all of this is because they believed, that is, they uttered the words of the testimony of faith and did what one does when entering Islam, and then they disbelieved. Their disbelief then became evident afterwards, through their saying: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are donkeys," and similar things. Or they uttered belief in front of the believers, then uttered disbelief in front of their devils, mocking Islam, as in His saying: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say: "We believe."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14], etc.

فَطُبِعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ (So a seal was set upon their hearts), that is, it was sealed over them, so that faith could not enter them, as a recompense for their hypocrisy.

فَهم لا يَفْقَهُونَ (so they do not understand), that is, they do not reflect, or they do not recognize the soundness of faith.

The discourse in "And when you see them, their bodies please you" is addressed to the Messenger of Allah, or to everyone who is addressed.

"And if they speak, you listen to their speech": Ibn Ubayy was a tall, handsome, eloquent man, and a group of hypocrites shared his description. They used to attend the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ and lean back in it. They had imposing appearances and eloquent tongues, so the Prophet ﷺ and those present were impressed by their physiques and listened to their speech.

As for the position of "as if they were blocks of wood propped up," it is in the nominative case, on the basis of "they are as if they were blocks of wood," or it is a resumed sentence with no grammatical place (of its own).

"Propped up" against the wall: in their reclining they are compared, while being nothing but empty bodies devoid of faith and good, to blocks of wood propped against a wall. This is because wood, when it is put to use, is placed in a roof, a wall, or other places of benefit; and as long as it is left unused and not benefited from, it is propped against a wall. So they are likened to it in being of no use. Or it is because they are shapes without spirits and bodies without understanding. "Khushb" (blocks of wood), according to Abu 'Amr, and not 'Abbas and 'Ali, is the plural of "khashabah," like "badanah" and "budn," and "khushub," like "thamarah" and "thumur."

"They think every cry is against them": "every cry" is the first object, and the second object is "against them," and the sentence is complete. That is, they think every cry is falling upon them and harmful to them, because of their cowardice and terror. That is, when a caller calls out in the army, or an animal escapes or a lost item is announced, they assume it is an attack upon them.

Then He said: "They are the enemy," that is, they are the perfect enemies, for the most hostile enemy is the deceptive enemy, who smiles at you while the disease of hatred lies beneath his ribs.

"So beware of them," and do not be deceived by their outward appearances.

"May Allah destroy them": it is a supplication against them, or an instruction to the believers that they should invoke this against them.

"How are they turned away?": how do they deviate from the truth? It is an expression of wonder at their ignorance and their misguidance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 63 (al-Munafiqun), verse 5:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside﴾, they twist them (ʿaṭafūhā) and incline them (amālūhā), turning away from that and in arrogance. "Lawwaw" (they twisted), with the lightened form (al-takhfīf), is read by Nafiʿ.

﴿And you see them turning away while they are arrogant﴾, from seeking excuse and seeking forgiveness. It is narrated that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ encountered the Banu al-Mustaliq at al-Muraysiʿ, which was their water, and defeated them, Jihjah ibn Saʿid, a hired man of ʿUmar, and Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of Ibn Ubayy, clashed over the water. Jihjah shouted, "O Muhajirun!" and Sinan shouted, "O Ansar!" Jiʿal, one of the poor Muhajirun, helped Jihjah and struck Sinan. ʿAbd Allah said to Jiʿal, "You are there too!" and said, "We have not accompanied Muhammad except to be struck! By Allah, our likeness and theirs is only as the saying goes: 'Fatten your dog and it will eat you.' Truly, by Allah, if we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it." By "the mightier" he meant himself, and by "the meaner" he meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he said to his people, "By Allah, if you withhold from Jiʿal and his kind the surplus of food, they will not mount your necks. So do not spend on them until they disperse from around Muhammad."

Zayd ibn Arqam, who was a youth, heard of this and said, "By Allah, you are the humble, the little, the hated among your people, while Muhammad, on his head is the crown of honour, in the might of the Most Merciful and the strength of the Muslims." ʿAbd Allah said, "Be silent, for I was only joking." Zayd informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite, O Messenger of Allah." He ﷺ said, "Then many noses in Yathrib would be made to tremble." ʿUmar said, "If you dislike that a Muhajir should kill him, then order an Ansari to do it." He ﷺ said, "Then how would it be when people say that Muhammad kills his companions?"

The Prophet ﷺ said to ʿAbd Allah, "Are you the one who spoke the words that reached me?" He said, "By Allah who sent down the Book to you, I did not say any of that, and Zayd is lying." This is His saying: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ [al-Mujadila: 16]. Those present said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is our elder and our chief; do not give credence to the words of a boy against him; perhaps he has made a mistake." When the revelation came down, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Zayd, "O boy, Allah has confirmed you and has belied the hypocrites." (p-487) When the lie of ʿAbd Allah became clear, it was said to him, "Severe verses have been revealed concerning you. Go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ so that he may ask forgiveness for you." He turned his head aside and said, "You ordered me to believe, and I believed; you ordered me to pay my zakat, and I paid it. There remains for me only to prostrate to Muhammad." Then there was revealed: "﴿And when it is said to them, 'Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you'﴾." He did not remain but a few days before he fell ill and died.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 6:

﴿It is the same for them whether you seek forgiveness for them or do not seek forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾ That is: as long as they remain upon hypocrisy. The meaning: it is the same for them whether seeking forgiveness or not seeking it, because they do not pay attention to it and do not regard it, due to their disbelief; or because Allah does not forgive them.

And it is read: "اسْتَغْفَرْتَ" (istaghfarta, "did you seek forgiveness"), with the interrogative particle elided, because the balanced "am" (ام, "or") indicates it.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the people who are defiantly disobedient﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 7:

﴿They are the ones who say: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse."﴾ "Yanfaddu" means they disperse, go their separate ways.

﴿And to Allah belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, to Him belong the provisions and the apportioning, so it is He who provides for them from them, even if the people of Madinah refuse to spend on them.

﴿But the hypocrites do not understand﴾: but ʿAbdullah (ibn Ubayy) and his like are ignorant, not understanding this, so they babble with what Satan makes attractive to them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 8:

﴿They say: "If we return to Madinah, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it."﴾ [That is, on return from the expedition against Banu al-Mustaliq.]

﴿But honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾: [honour here means] victory and strength; [it belongs] to whomever Allah has honoured and strengthened, from among His Messenger and the believers. They are the ones specially singled out for it, just as abasement and humiliation belong to Satan and his followers among the disbelievers and hypocrites. It is also related from one of the righteous, who was in a shabby state: "Am I not upon Islam, which is the honour with which there is no humiliation, and the wealth with which there is no poverty?!" And it is related from al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said to him: "People claim that there is arrogance (tīh) in you." He said: "It is not arrogance, rather it is dignity ('izzah)," and he recited this verse:

﴿But the hypocrites do not know.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 63, verse 9:

﴿O you who believe, let not﴾ — i.e., do not occupy you (lā tushghilkum),

﴿your wealth﴾ — and its disposal, and the striving in managing its affairs, by growing it and seeking profit,

﴿nor your children﴾ — and your delight in them, your compassion for them, and providing for their needs,

﴿divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ — i.e., from the five daily prayers, or from the Qur'an,

﴿And whoever does that﴾ — he intends being occupied with the worldly life over the religion. It was also said: whoever occupies himself with the increase of his wealth over managing his affairs, and with pleasing his children over reforming his final return (ma'ād),

﴿then those are the losers﴾ — in their trade, since they sold what remains for what perishes.

And spend out of what We have provided you, "min" (some of) being partitive, and the intended meaning of spending being: that which is obligatory,

before death comes to one of you, i.e., before he sees the signs of death and witnesses that which makes him despair of respite and makes spending impossible for him,

so that he says: "My Lord, why did You not delay me",
why did You not postpone my death,

"to a near term", to a little time,

"so that I would give charity" (fa-aṣṣaddaqa), i.e., so that I would give charity, and it is the answer to "why not" (lawlā),

"and I would be among the righteous", among the believers. The verse is about the believers, though it has been said it is about the hypocrites. "Wa-akūna" (and I would be), Abu 'Amr read it in the accusative, as a conjunction upon the wording, while the jussive is upon the position of "fa-aṣṣaddaqa", as if it were said: "If You delay me, I would give charity and I would be (righteous)."

Al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil (Commentary on surah 63, verse 11):

﴿And Allah will never delay a soul﴾ from death, ﴿when its term has come﴾, which is written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾. "Hammad and Yahya" (narration-chain names as they stand in the text, the transmitters' names in the chain).

The meaning is that when you know that delaying death beyond its appointed time is something no one can accomplish, and that it will certainly come upon you, and that Allah is All-Knowing of your deeds, and will therefore repay you for them, including for withholding what is obligatory and other things, then nothing remains but to hasten to discharge what is obligatory and to prepare for meeting Allah.
